basics.name: Amirhossein Ravari
basics.label: PhD Candidate · Reinforcement Learning, Human–AI Collaboration, Bayesian Inference
basics.summary: Ph.D. candidate in Electrical and Computer Engineering at Northeastern University working on reinforcement learning and Bayesian inference for human–AI collaboration. Research focuses on learning models of human decision-making and expert knowledge from limited behavioral data, using expert-enabled inference of hidden Markov models, inverse reinforcement learning conditioned on human factors, and multi-agent reinforcement learning under partial observability, with applications in cyber defense, disaster response, and biomedical sciences. Ten peer-reviewed publications (eight first-author) in venues including *Artificial Intelligence*, *IEEE Transactions on Artificial Intelligence*, *IEEE Control Systems Letters*, L4DC, ACC, and ICASSP. **Open to research internships and full-time positions for Spring and Summer 2027.**

work.name: Northeastern University
work.summary: Imani Lab, advised by Prof. Mahdi Imani.
highlights: Formulated expert-enabled Bayesian inference that models experts as imperfect reinforcement learning agents, incorporating expert-acquired data into the inference of hidden Markov models and biological regulatory networks.

Designed an adversarial inverse reinforcement learning algorithm conditioned on three human factors (fatigue, expertise, risk tolerance) to learn operator-specific defense policies, outperforming factor-oblivious baselines on CAGE Challenge 2.

Developed methods for learning humans’ implicit perception of complex, unknown environments and for inferring latent task models in human–AI collaboration under uncertainty, evaluated in simulated rescue tasks.
Built hybrid probabilistic models of heterogeneous human teams under partial observability that generalize centralized and decentralized models and outperform both at high rationality levels.

Developed a kernel-based inverse learning framework that infers individual defenders' latent cognitive traits (e.g., risk tolerance, curiosity) from limited behavioral data, validated on 108 participants across 26 cybersecurity scenarios; personalized models exceeded 0.8 action-prediction similarity versus at most 0.6 for a group-level RL baseline, and estimated traits more accurately than GPT-4o and an LSTM-encoder baseline.

Contributed to posterior-conditioned multi-agent reinforcement learning for adaptive cyber defense, in which decentralized defenders condition on an attack-context belief inferred online, evaluated on the CAGE-4 testbed.

work.name: Northeastern University LEADERs Program
work.position: LEADERs Fellow, data science research project with Walkky
work.summary: Northeastern-funded fellowship supporting dissertation-related research with Walkky, a startup partner in the university's LEADERs program.
highlights: Co-developed RhythmBERT, a self-supervised ECG language model pretrained on ~800,000 unlabeled ECG recordings from 161,352 patients; using only Lead II, it improved AUROC by ~4.5% over the next-best 12-lead baseline on CPSC2018.
Researched multimodal LLMs that combine ECG signals, echocardiograms, and clinical reports into unified representations for cardiovascular disease detection.
Implemented a Vision Transformer ensemble (bagging with majority voting) for ECG image classification, reaching 82% accuracy.
